disease_label_per_paper: Acute liver failure treated with high-volume plasmapheresis
presentation_summary: 28-year-old woman with polysubstance abuse history was admitted with altered mental status and last known normal one day before admission.
On arrival she was hypotensive at 89/53 mmHg, hypoxic with oxygen saturation 74%, afebrile, encephalopathic with GCS 8, intubated for airway protection, and started on norepinephrine after fluids.

Initial labs showed hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, WBC 11.2 x10^9/L, platelets 115 x10^9/L, AST 5181 U/L, ALT 6633 U/L, ALP 92 U/L, total bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL, INR 2.7, creatinine 2.16 mg/dL, and ammonia 94 umol/L.
Urine drug screen was positive for cocaine and benzodiazepines; acetaminophen, salicylate, ethanol, hepatitis serologies, infectious workup, CT head, and hepatic duplex were unrevealing or negative.

Course included oliguric renal failure with hyperkalemia requiring SLED/CRRT, DIC requiring cryoprecipitate and FFP, myocardial injury, AST/ALT over 10000 U/L within 24 hours, NAC, and high-volume plasmapheresis started day 2 with clinical and biochemical improvement.
